title: kumiko codemod lists package-merge
detail: kumiko codemod package-merge rewrites imports and package.json dependencies of merged packages.

title: project rebuild keeps blind indexes and aborts without crypto, events prune names its aggregate types
detail: `kumiko project rebuild` now wires the subject KMS and blind-index key from the env like `schema apply` and `ops backfill-pii`, so rebuilding a PII projection no longer nulls its bidx columns. Without the crypto env an app with PII fields aborts the rebuild unless `--allow-plaintext-pii <reason>` is passed. `kumiko events prune` takes the required `--aggregate-types <a,b>` flag; before, it always failed because pruneEvents needs explicit aggregate types.

title: kumiko ports and sync-managed use the shared port reader and print managed warnings
detail: kumiko ports reads from repo-manifest/app-ports; check managed and sync-managed print the infraRef warning.

title: kumiko codemod lists and runs codemods
detail: kumiko codemod lists the codemods without a name. kumiko codemod <name> runs one against the current directory as a dry run and applies it with --write.

title: kumiko ops backfill-pii encrypts plaintext PII events of the app in kumiko.config.ts
detail: kumiko ops backfill-pii [--dry-run] [--resolve-owner-from-projection] [--rekey-tenant-keyed-owner-fields] [--erase-unresolvable-subjects] runs the framework PII backfill over the features of kumiko.config.ts with DATABASE_URL, PLATFORM_KEK (and PLATFORM_KEK_PREVIOUS) and KUMIKO_BLIND_INDEX_KEY from the environment. It does not rebuild projections; run kumiko ops backfill-pii --rebuild afterwards, which rebuilds only the projections of entities with personal fields. A second backfill run changes nothing. Apps with their own backfill-pii script switch to this command and to the two-step runbook.

title: kumiko check gains the managed and scripts steps; new kumiko sync-managed and kumiko ports
detail: kumiko check managed compares framework-owned files with the installed templates and prints a diff; files with a local marker are skipped and listed. kumiko check scripts requires dev, build, start, typecheck, lint, check, test, test:unit, test:integration, test:integration:ci, test:dom (with uiRoots), test:real, e2e, e2e:real, screenshots and prepare, and lists extras. Both steps fail only once the app calls defineAppConfig. kumiko check accepts step ids as positional filters (kumiko check managed scripts). kumiko sync-managed [--write] [--adopt] writes the templates; it never overwrites a file without marker unless --adopt is passed, never touches local files and refuses symlinked paths. kumiko ports [workspace-root] lists the ports of every app below the root and exits 1 on a collision. kumiko agent lint also checks prodFeatures.

title: kumiko handbuch build refuses a dangerous --out; missing-peer message tells an outdated install from a missing one
detail: handbuch build deletes the output directory before building, so `--out .` or `--out <root>` removed the checkout. The command now exits 2 when --out is, or contains, the working directory, --root or a configured source repo. When an installed @cosmicdrift package lacks a requested subpath, the error asks for an upgrade instead of recommending bun add.

title: kumiko handbuch build generates the user manual from a JSON config
detail:
New command `kumiko handbuch build` generates the user manual as a static page from a JSON config
`kumiko handbuch build <config.json> [--root <dir>] [--out <dir>] [--shots <dir>] [--texts <dir>] [--web-shots <dir>] [--web-texts <dir>] [--web-repo <dir>] [--repo <dir>] [--locale <l>] [--no-large]`. Relative config paths resolve against `--root` (default: the working directory); the default output is `<root>/.handbuch/<config-name>`. Image conversion needs `sharp`, which is an optional peer dependency: without it the command prints an install hint and exits 1. The command also needs the app's `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework` and `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-headless` (optional peers, loaded only when `handbuch build` runs). Replaces the workspace handbuch builder script.

title: kumiko-cli declares framework and bundled-features as optional peer dependencies
detail: kumiko-cli declares @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features as optional peer dependencies instead of hard dependencies, so `kumiko new app` no longer pulls them in; commands that need them report a missing install instead of a resolver stacktrace

title: kumiko-cli optional peers no longer force a 1.0.0 release
detail: kumiko-cli declares its optional peers framework and bundled-features with an explicit 0.x range, and changesets only bumps peer dependents when that range is left, so a minor framework release no longer pushes the fixed package group to 1.0.0

title: kumiko-upgrade ships with kumiko-cli and takes the installed version from the repo's own install or bun.lock
detail:
`kumiko-upgrade` ships with kumiko-cli and reads the repo's own version
Repos that depend only on `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-cli` and `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-guards` now get the `kumiko-upgrade` bin, which the upgrade-state guard runs. The installed version comes from the repo itself: its `node_modules`, the framework's package directories, then its `bun.lock`. It no longer walks up into a parent workspace, and with the isolated linker `installedVersion` is no longer `null`. Changelog entries newer than the installed version are not reported as pending, even when a parent workspace holds a newer install.

title: kumiko check requires uiRoots for kind "app"
detail:
`kumiko check` fails a kind "app" without uiRoots
A repo with `kind: "app"` and no `uiRoots` used to skip the UI guards silently. `kumiko check` (also with `--explain`) now prints an error and exits 1 before any step runs. Declare `uiRoots`, or set `uiRoots: []` for an app without UI; the step list then shows that the UI guards are skipped on purpose. A repo that relies on the derived manifest also gets the hint to add a `kumiko.json`. Other kinds are unchanged. `kumiko new app` now writes a `kumiko.json` with `uiRoots: ["src/features/*/web"]`.
migration:
Add `uiRoots` to the `kumiko.json` of every `kind: "app"` repo, for example `["src/app", "src/features/*/web"]`, or `[]` for an app without UI. A repo without a `kumiko.json` needs one first, since the derived manifest cannot declare uiRoots.
Workspace state at release: kumiko-platform, offlot-app, phronexsis and show-pony declare `kind: "app"` without `uiRoots`.

title: project and consumer validate the subcommand before any database work
detail: `kumiko project` and `kumiko consumer` now reject an unknown or missing subcommand with the usage text before importing the config or touching the database. A failing state-table DDL no longer leaks the connection pool and is reported as an error with exit code 1.

title: kumiko check runs boot validation against the repo root when started from a subdirectory
detail: `kumiko check` now runs the boot validation against the repo root instead of the current directory, so running it from a subdirectory no longer reports a missing `kumiko/schema.ts`.

title: kumiko check survives throwing steps, config loading validates its shape
detail: `kumiko check` counts a step that throws as a failure and still runs the remaining steps, and `--explain` now returns the guards' exit code. The `agent`, `consumer` and `project` commands report a readable message when `kumiko.config.ts` has no default export with a `features` array instead of crashing. Invalid-manifest errors name the root as `<root>` instead of an empty path.

title: New `kumiko check`: boot validation plus the guard suites in one command, step list derived from kumiko.json
detail: Until now every consumer repo assembled the same chain by hand — `kumiko-schema validate` plus `kumiko-guards guards|ui|checks` in package.json, CI YAML or check-wt.sh, in four different shapes, each with its own hand-written presence gate (`|| true`, `::error::`, `bun add --no-save`). `kumiko check` derives the step list declaratively from the kumiko.json manifest instead: `kind: "app"` adds boot validation (validateBoot over the composed FEATURES in kumiko/schema.ts), any kind other than "tooling" adds the AST guards and the repo checks, declared uiRoots add the UI guards, and a "tooling" repo says out loud that it has nothing to check. `--explain` prints the resolved step list with the reason for each step and passes through to the guards own --explain without running a suite. When @cosmicdrift/kumiko-guards cannot be loaded the command fails with an install hint instead of skipping silently.
migration: No action required — additive. A repo that today calls `kumiko-schema validate` and `kumiko-guards guards|ui|checks` separately in package.json, CI YAML or check-wt.sh replaces that chain with `bun kumiko check`; the step list then follows from kumiko.json (kind, uiRoots) instead of from the script. Private bins without a public counterpart (kumiko-guard-comment-lang, kumiko-guard-ui) stay as their own step next to it for now.

title: `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-cli/repo-manifest`: kumiko.json repo manifest schema and loader (fw#2856).
detail: repoManifestSchema declares kind (a role — framework|library|app, not a layout description) plus repo-relative sourceRoots/testGlobs/uiRoots/excludes patterns; loadRepoManifest reads and validates a repo's kumiko.json, rejecting absolute paths, ".." traversal, and symlinks that resolve outside the repo root, and is strict against unknown fields (typos fail loudly instead of being silently ignored). Without a kumiko.json it falls back to deriving a layout from packages/*/src or src/ and warns once via the injected warn option.
